Hi Lindsey —

Thanks for the clear list. I've attached a first-pass cost model (aurora_map_cost_model_v1.xlsx) and a short "MAP econ smoke tests" doc. Quick answers inline below, then internal notes.

1) Tokens/$ baseline: the hosted numbers you quoted are aligned with our model but they assume:
   - sequence length distribution: median request 160 tokens, 90th perc 480 tokens
   - sampling: temp 0.7, top_p 0.95 (these change decoding cost slightly but not materially)
   - the hosted figure includes prefix compression for repeated system prompts; dedicated assumes higher throughput and better kernel selection (hence lower tokens/$).

2) Caching & batching:
   - Prefix/KV caching: we enable prefix caching by default for the system prompt + onboarding templates; customer-visible caching configurable via MAP.
   - Batching window: default continuous-batching target is 8–12 ms additional latency per request, with adaptive batching up to 50 ms under high concurrency.
   - For Aurora, we recommend enabling prefix caching and a conservative batching policy (target 20–25 ms) to keep tail latency predictable for clinical flows.

3) Demo cutoff: to qualify for pilot pricing in the MAP, we need acceptance testing completed by Friday, 2028-07-20. That gives us two weeks for the smoke tests and one week buffer for fixes.

Attached: aurora_map_cost_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — includes tokens-per-call scenarios, caching on/off, batching latencies.

Next steps: Ben, Karthik, Neha — can you review the model and the proposed smoke-test plan? I'll loop Vivek if we need a short kernel/quantization tweak for the dedicated variant.

- Prefetch/kV warmers: propose a scheduled prefetch during off-peak to reduce cold-start cost for known clinical templates.

Ben — adding technical constraints from runtime:

- Batching tradeoffs: for Aurora's request profile (p95 seq len ~420 tokens), an aggressive batching window (50 ms) improves throughput & reduces tokens/$ by ~12% but increases p99 latency by ~80 ms — worth quantifying for their SLOs.
- KV cache eviction: default LRU with size tuned to expected template set; if Aurora uses many unique prompts, caching benefit drops. Recommend we ask Aurora for a small sample of representative prompts (10–50) so we can estimate cache hit rate in the model.
- Evaluation runs: propose we run three batch jobs across representative traffic (low/med/high concurrency) and capture tokens-per-call distributions, tail latency, and cost per 1k requests. We'll provide those artifacts for the MAP.

I'll prepare the eval job spec and a short timeline.
